nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Environmental and occupational health|Climate change impacts_qna_000
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the implication of climate change on the management of persistent organic pollutants as per the document?
nodes.answer: Consideration needs to be given to the impacts of climate change on the behavior and risks associated with POPs over extended timescales.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Environmental and occupational health|Climate change impacts_qna_001
nodes.question: How is the Austrian labour market influenced by climate policy May, as described in the expert report of GWS?
nodes.answer: According to the expert report of GWS, climate policy May had a positive effect on the Austrian labour market by creating new workplaces, especially in the area of renewable energies and sustainable mobile.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Environmental and occupational health|Climate change impacts_qna_002
nodes.question: How were the costs of accidents, air pollution, climate change, and other external factors calculated in the analysis?
nodes.answer: The costs for accidents, air pollution, climate change, noise, well-to-tank emissions, and habitat damage were calculated based on the findings of Essen et al. (2019).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Environmental and occupational health|Climate change impacts_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the short-run effects of high temperatures on exports according to the study?
nodes.answer: The study finds that a month with an average temperature above 30°C leads to export losses of around three percent, with these effects increasing in the labour-intensity of exports.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Environmental and occupational health|Climate change impacts_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How do exporter characteristics influence the effect size of temperature impacts on exports?
nodes.answer: The impact rises with the labour-intensity of the exports.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Environmental and occupational health|Climate change impacts_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What factors are suggested to govern short-run temperature impacts on exports?
nodes.answer: Labour productivity or labour supply effects in the exporting country due to physiological heat stress are suggested to govern short-run temperature impacts on exports.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Environmental and occupational health|Climate change impacts_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What does the study by Zivin and Neidell (2014) suggest regarding labour supply in climate-exposed industries?
nodes.answer: The study suggests that there is a substantial reduction of labour supply in climate-exposed industries on days with high temperatures.
